questions.enonce_markdown: A good example of an incorporated business unit is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
An incorporated business is one that has been registered as a separate legal person, distinct from its owners: it can own property, sue and be sued in its own name, and its shareholders enjoy limited liability. A joint stock company (limited company) is the typical example. A sole proprietor and a partnership are unincorporated: the owners and the business are legally the same person, and the owners are personally liable for the debts. A cooperative society is registered under the cooperative law as a society of members and is not the standard example of an incorporated unit in this syllabus.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A perfectly inelastic demand curve will be;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Perfectly inelastic demand means that the quantity demanded does not change at all when the price changes (elasticity of demand equals zero). On a diagram with price on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal axis, the same quantity is demanded at every price, so the curve is a straight **vertical** line. A horizontal curve is perfectly elastic demand, and a normal demand curve is downward sloping.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
This question is based on the cost schedule below;

| Output (units) | Total cost (Fcfa) |
|---|---|
| 0 | 1000 |
| 1 | 2500 |
| 2 | 6000 |
| 3 | 9600 |

What is the fixed cost of the second unit of output produced?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fixed costs do not change with the level of output: they have to be paid even when nothing is produced. At an output of 0 units the total cost is 1000 Fcfa, and this cost is entirely fixed (there are no variable costs when nothing is produced). So the fixed cost is 1000 Fcfa at every level of output, including the second unit.

Check: variable cost of 2 units = $6000 - 1000 = 5000$ Fcfa, which does change with output.

Traps: 3500 is the increase in total cost from 1 to 2 units (marginal cost), not a fixed cost; 2400 and 2000 are not read from the table.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The low level of industrialization in Cameroon is caused by;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Industrialization needs good roads, railways, ports, reliable electricity and water supply. Where these are inadequate, production and transport costs are high and investors are discouraged, so industry grows slowly. Immigration, skilled labour and abundant raw materials are favourable factors for industry, so they cannot explain a *low* level of industrialization.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most profitable function of a commercial bank is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A commercial bank earns most of its income from the interest charged on the loans and overdrafts it grants, which is higher than the interest it pays to depositors. Accepting deposits is its basic function but it brings costs, not profit; keeping valuables and night safe facilities bring only small fees.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Contractual payments made to owners of land and capital are ;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A contractual payment is a fixed sum agreed in advance and paid whatever the profit of the firm. Rent is the contractual reward of land and interest is the contractual reward of capital. A dividend is not contractual: it is a share of profit and depends on how well the company does. Wages reward labour, not land or capital.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A man has a monthly income of 200,000 frs and the tax rate is 5%. Determine his disposable income?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Disposable income is income left after direct taxes have been paid.

Tax = $5\% \times 200\,000 = 10\,000$ Fcfa.

Disposable income = $200\,000 - 10\,000 = 190\,000$ Fcfa.

Traps: 10,000 is the tax itself; 210,000 adds the tax instead of subtracting it.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A perfect definition of "demand" must contain the following;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Demand is the quantity of a good that consumers are willing and able to buy at a given price **during a given period of time**. A complete definition therefore needs three elements: the price, the quantity and the time period (for example per week or per month). Without the time period, a quantity bought has no meaning.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A principle of taxation that requires that the tax yield be more than the cost of collection, is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Adam Smith's canons (principles) of taxation are equity, certainty, convenience and economy. The canon of **economy** says that the cost of collecting a tax must be small compared with the revenue it yields, otherwise it is not worth collecting. Certainty means that the taxpayer knows how much, when and how to pay; convenience means paying at a suitable time and in a suitable way; equity means fairness according to ability to pay.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The documents given to company promoters by the registrar of companies are;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The promoters send the memorandum of association and the articles of association to the registrar of companies. If everything is in order, the registrar **gives back** the certificate of incorporation (the company now exists as a legal person) and, for a public company that has met the capital requirements, the certificate of trading (permission to start business). The memorandum, the articles and the prospectus are documents prepared by the promoters themselves and sent to the registrar, not given by him.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Certificate of incorporations and certificate of trading
Memorandum of association and article of association

questions.enonce_markdown: When the government through the central bank, decides to reduce the supply of money in an economy, the objective will likely be;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Reducing the money supply (for example by raising the bank rate or selling securities) leaves people and firms with less money to spend, so total demand falls and prices stop rising. The objective is therefore to curb (control) inflation. To promote growth or reduce unemployment the government would increase the money supply, and income redistribution is done mainly through taxes and transfers.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If an increase in the price of good X leads to an increase in the demand for good Y, goods X and Y represent;
questions.corrige_markdown:
When the price of X rises, consumers switch to Y, so the demand for Y increases: X and Y are substitutes. Goods that are substitutes are said to be in **competitive demand**. Joint demand applies to complements (such as a car and petrol): a rise in the price of X would then *reduce* the demand for Y. Derived demand is demand for a factor because of the demand for the good it produces, and composite demand is demand for a good with several uses.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The population where by a greater proportion is made up more of the young and adult is referred to as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A population with a large share of young people and adults of reproductive age has a high birth rate and keeps increasing: it is a **growing population**. An ageing population is the opposite, with a rising share of old people. Underpopulation compares population with resources, not with age. A working population is only the part of the population that is able and willing to work, and it excludes the young.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The inability for a teacher in Yaounde to become a lawyer in Bamenda is brought about by;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A teacher in Yaounde cannot simply become a lawyer in Bamenda because the two jobs need different qualifications: this is **occupational immobility** of labour, caused by the long period of training that a lawyer needs. The other options (housing costs, social ties, children's education) are causes of *geographical* immobility, that is, difficulty in moving from Yaounde to Bamenda, not of the change of occupation.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How many denominations of coins does the FCFA have?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Central African franc (FCFA) is issued in coins of 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 and 500 francs, that is **eight** denominations (the notes are a separate set). The smallest coins are rarely used in daily trade.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The composition of the national debt of a country is as follows;
Loans from IMF ___ 2 billion Fcfa
Loans from institutions within the country ___ 1 billion Fcfa
Loans from friendly countries ___ 3 billion Fcfa
Loans from citizens who bought treasury bills ___ 2 billion Fcfa
What is the percentage of internal debts?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Internal debt is money owed to lenders inside the country; external debt is owed to foreign lenders.

- Internal: institutions within the country (1 billion) + citizens who bought treasury bills (2 billion) = 3 billion Fcfa.
- External: IMF (2 billion) + friendly countries (3 billion) = 5 billion Fcfa.
- Total debt = $3 + 5 = 8$ billion Fcfa.

Percentage of internal debt = $\frac{3}{8} \times 100 = 37.5\%$.

Trap: 62.5% is the share of the *external* debt.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When the government takes over a private business venture to manage and control ,we call it;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Nationalization is the transfer of a privately owned business to the state, which then manages and controls it. Privatization and denationalization are the opposite: the state sells public enterprises to private owners. "Takeover bid" is a different idea, the offer of one company to buy the shares of another.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A customer has 200,000Fcfa in his current account and withdraws 250,000fcfa. If the rate of interest of the bank is 10% , how much interest will the customer pay?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The customer withdraws more than he has, so the account is overdrawn. Overdraft = $250\,000 - 200\,000 = 50\,000$ Fcfa. Interest is charged on the overdraft only, not on the whole amount withdrawn:

Interest = $10\% \times 50\,000 = 5\,000$ Fcfa.

Traps: 25,000 is 10% of the 250,000 withdrawn; 20,000 is 10% of the balance of 200,000.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A large firm has the ability to employ expert sales men and expert buyers, such a firm is said to be enjoying;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Economies of scale are the fall in average cost as a firm grows larger. Expert buyers who purchase raw materials in bulk at low prices and expert salesmen who sell and advertise the products efficiently are advantages in buying and selling: these are **marketing economies**. Technical economies concern machinery and production methods, managerial economies concern specialist managers, and financial economies concern cheaper credit.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When a country sells goods cheaper abroad than in the home market, this is termed;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Dumping is the sale of goods in a foreign market at a price lower than the price in the home market (often below cost). Smuggling and contraband goods concern illegal trade that avoids customs duties, and an auction is a sale to the highest bidder.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The act of giving different names to products to make them appear different, is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Product differentiation is the process of making products that are basically similar appear different in the mind of the consumer, for example by giving them different names, brands, packaging or advertising. The key words are "to make them appear different". Packaging is only the wrapping of a product, branding is the giving of a name or trademark, and standardization is making products identical, which is the opposite.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the problems faced by agriculture in Cameroon is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Under the traditional land tenure system, land is often held by families or communities and shared among heirs, so farms are small and scattered and farmers cannot easily use land as security to borrow money or invest in it. This is a well-known problem of Cameroonian agriculture. Availability of chemicals and availability of capital would be advantages, not problems.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The regular organization of trade fairs in the economy of Cameroon is an example of;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trade fairs encourage producers and consumers to meet and promote local products, but the government does not itself produce, fix prices or control any good: it only creates favourable conditions for the market to work. This is **indirect intervention**. Direct intervention would be, for example, price controls or state ownership. Fiscal policy uses taxes and spending, and monetary policy uses money supply and interest rates.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The term "ends" as used in the definition of economics, refers to;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Economics is defined as the study of how scarce means (resources) with alternative uses are allocated to satisfy unlimited **ends** (human wants). The "means" are the economic resources; the "ends" are the wants that people try to satisfy.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most important characteristic of money is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Whatever its form, something can serve as money only if people are ready to accept it in payment for goods and services and in settlement of debts. Acceptability is therefore the most important characteristic; portability, divisibility and uniformity make money more convenient but are secondary.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Trade between Cameroon and China only, is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bilateral trade is trade between two countries only, here Cameroon and China. Multilateral trade involves more than two countries. Foreign trade and international trade are general terms for trade between countries and do not say how many countries are involved.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Village X has a population of 10000 people in January 20XX, during the year 2000 people moved into and 1000 people moved out of the village, also there were 1500 recorded live births and 500 recorded deaths. Determine the population at the end of the year?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Population change = natural increase + net migration.

- Natural increase = births - deaths = $1500 - 500 = 1000$.
- Net migration = immigrants - emigrants = $2000 - 1000 = 1000$.

Population at the end of the year = $10\,000 + 1000 + 1000 = 12\,000$ people.

Traps: 13,000 forgets the people who moved out (or the deaths); 13,500 adds the births and the immigrants only.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given quantity demanded to be 400-P and quantity supplied to be 40 + P, where P is price of the good in Fcfa. Calculate the equilibrium price?
questions.corrige_markdown:
At equilibrium, quantity demanded equals quantity supplied:

$400 - P = 40 + P$

$400 - 40 = 2P$

$360 = 2P$, so $P = 180$ Fcfa.

Check: $Q_d = 400 - 180 = 220$ and $Q_s = 40 + 180 = 220$. The equilibrium quantity is 220, which is the trap in option A (that is a quantity, not the price).

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One reason for measuring National Income is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
National income per head, measured at constant prices, is used to compare the standard of living of different countries (and of the same country over time), to judge economic growth, and to plan. The unemployment rate and the inflation rate are measured by other statistics (labour force surveys and price indexes), and tax revenue is determined by tax rates and the tax base.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: To determine the rate of unemployment
To determine the rate of inflation
To compare standard of living between two countries

questions.enonce_markdown: The possible amalgamation between Guinness Cameroon SA and Brasseries du Cameroun is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Both firms are brewers, so they are at the same stage of production of the same product. A merger between firms of the same industry at the same stage is **horizontal integration**. Vertical integration joins firms at different stages (for example a brewery and a barley farm), and lateral (diversified) integration joins firms in different but related or unrelated lines of business.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An indicator of economic development is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Economic development is measured by indicators such as real income per head (income per capita adjusted for price changes), life expectancy and literacy. Among the options, high real per capita income is the standard economic indicator. A high level of technology and industrialization are means or features of development, and an increase in the standard of living is what development means rather than a measure of it.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The immediate effect of a maximum price instituted by the government is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A maximum price (price ceiling) is set below the equilibrium price to protect consumers. At that price the quantity demanded is higher than the quantity supplied, so there is an immediate **shortage**. Queues, rationing and the black market are later consequences of the shortage. A surplus results from a minimum price above equilibrium.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The object on which a tax is placed is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The tax base is the object (income, goods, property, transaction) on which a tax is charged. The tax rate is the percentage or amount charged on the base. Tax evasion is illegal non-payment and tax avoidance is the legal arrangement of one's affairs to pay less tax.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A population pyramid with a broad base is typical of ;

*Options as printed:* A) Developed country   B) Under developed country   C) Developing country   D) Advanced country
questions.corrige_markdown:
A broad base means a large proportion of young children, which comes from a high birth rate. This is typical of poorer countries, which are described as developing (less developed) countries. Developed (advanced) countries have low birth rates, so their pyramids have a narrow base and are almost rectangular.

The options "under developed" and "developing" describe the same type of country in most O Level books, so two options are acceptable.

**Intended answer: C (Developing country).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The composition for the demand of money for an individual is as follows;
Transaction balance---- 150,000fcfa
Precautionary balance -----50,000fcfa
Speculative balance----100,000fcfa
Determine the active balance to this individual?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Active balances are the money held to be spent: the transactions balance plus the precautionary balance. The speculative balance is held waiting for a profitable investment and is an idle balance.

Active balance = $150\,000 + 50\,000 = 200\,000$ Fcfa.

Traps: 250,000 adds the speculative balance to the transactions balance; 150,000 is the transactions balance alone.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One factor affecting elasticity of supply is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Elasticity of supply measures how far the quantity supplied responds to a change in price. Producers can respond quickly when they hold stocks of the good, so availability of stocks makes supply more elastic. The other three options (substitutes, degree of necessity, proportion of income spent) are determinants of the elasticity of *demand*.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A limitation of division of labour is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Adam Smith said that the division of labour is limited by the extent of the market. If the market is small, the quantity that can be sold is small and it is not worthwhile to employ many specialised workers. Monotony, fatigue and boredom are disadvantages of division of labour (they affect the worker), not what limits how far it can be carried.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A determinant of the size of a country's national income is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The size of national income depends on the quantity and quality of the factors of production available. A country with a large stock of natural resources (land, minerals, forests, oil) can produce more. The standard of living is a result of national income, not a cause; the level of prices affects the money value but not the real size; exports are only one component of national income.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Level of prices in the economy

questions.enonce_markdown: The production decisions in a mixed economy are taken by;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A mixed economy combines a public sector and a private sector, so what to produce is decided partly by the government (public enterprises) and partly by private individuals and firms. The price mechanism alone is a market economy; public authorities alone is a command economy; private individuals alone is again a market economy.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A measure of trade restriction that provokes retaliation from trade partners is;

*Options as printed:* A) Tariffs   B) Quotas   C) Embargo   D) Exchange control
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trade restrictions raise the price of imports or limit their quantity, so the exporting countries lose sales and may answer with restrictions of their own. Tariffs (taxes on imports) are the classic example discussed in textbooks, but quotas, embargoes and exchange controls can provoke retaliation too, so the key is not unique.

**Intended answer: A (Tariffs).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: When income elasticity of demand is negative, the good is said to be;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A negative income elasticity of demand means that the quantity demanded falls when income rises, as consumers switch to better goods (for example, from cheap gari to rice). Such a good is an **inferior good**. A normal or superior good has a positive income elasticity. A Giffen good is a special inferior good defined by a positive price elasticity of demand, not by income elasticity.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the various cost items incurred by a farmer in producing cassava and answer the question that follow;

| Items | Amount in Fcfa |
|---|---|
| Land | 5000 |
| Farm tools | 38,000 |
| Seedlings | 6000 |
| Insecticides | 11,000 |
| Wages | 20,000 |

Calculate the value of total fixed cost?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fixed costs are the costs of inputs that do not change with the quantity produced in the short run: here land and farm tools. Seedlings, insecticides and wages vary with the amount of cassava grown, so they are variable costs.

Total fixed cost = $5000 + 38\,000 = 43\,000$ Fcfa.

Check: total variable cost = $6000 + 11\,000 + 20\,000 = 37\,000$ Fcfa, which is the trap in option A; total cost = $80\,000$ Fcfa.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The table below shows the production possibilities for 2 countries with a given set of resources and level of technology.

| Country | Cocoa(tons) | Coffee(tons) |
|---|---|---|
| A | 100 | 50 |
| B | 85 | 150 |

Using the absolute advantage theory, determine the output of cocoa after specialization?

*Options as printed:* A) 200 tons of Cocoa   B) 370 tons of Cocoa   C) 15 tons of Cocoa   D) 185 tons of Cocoa
questions.corrige_markdown:
Absolute advantage means being able to produce a good with fewer resources, that is, more output from the same resources. Country A produces more cocoa than B (100 against 85) and B produces more coffee than A (150 against 50), so A should specialise in cocoa and B in coffee.

If each country shares its resources equally between the two goods (the usual assumption of this textbook example), A puts all its resources into cocoa and doubles its cocoa output to $2 \times 100 = 200$ tons, while B makes no cocoa. The output of cocoa after specialization is 200 tons (and coffee is $2 \times 150 = 300$ tons).

Trap: 185 tons is the total cocoa before specialization ($100 + 85$).

The table does not say how the resources are shared, so this reading rests on an assumption.

**Intended answer: A (200 tons of Cocoa).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The central bank can reduce the amount of money in circulation by;
questions.corrige_markdown:
To reduce the money supply, the central bank uses a tight (restrictive) monetary policy: it sells securities, raises the bank rate and increases special deposits. Raising the bank rate makes borrowing dearer, so commercial banks lend less and credit shrinks. Buying securities, reducing special deposits and reducing bank rates all put more money into circulation.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Buying securities in the open market

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of primary production is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Primary production is the extraction of natural resources from the earth, sea or forest: farming, fishing, mining and lumbering (felling trees). Teaching, banking and hairdressing are services, which belong to tertiary production.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An aspect of government expenditure is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Government expenditure is the money the government spends, for example on public goods (roads, defence) and merit goods (education, health). Raising revenue, payment of taxes and contributions to social insurance funds are all ways in which the government *receives* money, so they are aspects of revenue.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Production of public and merit goods

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the ways that big plantations assist small holders is ;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Large plantations have the research facilities and capital to produce improved varieties, so they supply small farmers with improved seeds and seedlings, and often with technical advice and a market for their crops. Selling at very low prices, giving land and giving interest-free loans are not normal practice for a commercial business.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Selling to them at very low prices
Providing them with improved seed and seedlings

questions.enonce_markdown: By belonging to CEMAC, Cameroon enjoys;
questions.corrige_markdown:
CEMAC (Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa) is a regional grouping with free movement of goods and a common external tariff. Member states, including Cameroon, can sell their products to the whole community, so they enjoy **larger markets** and can benefit from economies of scale. The other options are not direct benefits of the membership.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Consider the following scores recorded by 10 students during an end of course economics test; 17,5,7,11,20,13,11,9,19,17. What is the median score?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The median is the middle value when the scores are arranged in order.

Ordered scores: 5, 7, 9, 11, 11, 13, 17, 17, 19, 20.

There are 10 scores (an even number), so the median is the mean of the 5th and 6th values: $\frac{11 + 13}{2} = 12$.

Traps: 12.9 is the mean of all the scores ($129 \div 10$); 13 is the 6th value alone.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One disadvantage of economic growth is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rapid economic growth increases total demand and may push prices up (inflation); it can also cause pollution and depletion of resources. Employment and an even distribution of income are benefits, and idle resources describe the opposite of growth.

**Answer: C.**
